title: A Leave-One-Park-Out Evaluation of Prithvi-EO-2.0 for Natura 2000 Grassland Habitat Segmentation
content: Periodic condition assessment of Natura 2000 (N2K)—the EU's network of protected areas under the Habitats Directive—is legally mandated but cannot be sustained at the required spatial scale through field survey alone. We introduce a multi-country Leave-One-Park-Out (LOPO) evaluation framework for binary per-habitat segmentation of N2K grasslands from Sentinel-2 multitemporal imagery, implemented using a parameter-efficient adaptation of the Prithvi-EO-2.0 geospatial foundation model. The framework spans four protected areas across Spain, Portugal, and France and three European biogeographic regions. Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) adapters (r=16, 6.3 M trainable parameters) fine-tune the frozen ViT-L backbone alongside a UPerNet decoder, ingesting three stochastically sampled monthly composites per training iteration. LOPO evaluation on three habitat configurations—semi-natural calcareous and Nardus grasslands (6210+6230), lowland and mountain hay meadows (6510+6520), and thermo-Mediterranean grasslands (6220)—assesses cross-park generalisation across ecologically distinct parks, with mean LOPO mIoU of 45.8% for 6210+6230 and 52.2% for 6510+6520 following a controlled data-expansion experiment that increases habitat-positive supervision by a factor of 25.3. A same-architecture within-park baseline inflates mean mIoU by 14.0 pp, directly quantifying the optimistic bias of conventional single-site evaluation.
